# fiat-crypto (vendored subset)

Formally verified field arithmetic generated by
[fiat-crypto](https://github.com/mit-plv/fiat-crypto) (MIT, Apache-2.0,
or BSD-1-Clause at our option; see `COPYRIGHT` and the `LICENSE-*`
files). Used by the native TLS library's P-256 signer,
`third_party/mbedtls/xo/xo_p256.c` (decision 0134).

- Commit: `f3ecb2cf1f771de34771e967193ee7f0ee0b0acf` (master on
  2026-10-10, committed 2026-10-09).
- Files, unmodified, with the SHA-256 of each in `SHA256SUMS`:
  - `src/p256_64.c` (upstream `fiat-c/src/p256_64.c`): Montgomery
    arithmetic modulo P-256's prime p = 2^256 - 2^224 + 2^192 + 2^96 - 1,
    64 bit words.
  - `src/p256_scalar_64.c` (upstream `fiat-c/src/p256_scalar_64.c`): the
    same modulo the group order n, for ECDSA's scalar arithmetic.
  - `COPYRIGHT`, `LICENSE-MIT`, `LICENSE-APACHE`, `LICENSE-BSD-1`,
    `AUTHORS`.
- How they were chosen: the signer needs multiplication, squaring,
  addition, subtraction, conversions, and constant time selection modulo
  p and n; both files provide them (generated by
  `word_by_word_montgomery --inline --static --use-value-barrier`, every
  function `static inline`, masks behind an empty `asm` barrier). Only
  the 64 bit variants: every native host is 64 bit (darwin/arm64,
  linux/arm64, linux/amd64) and clang has `unsigned __int128`. The 32
  bit files, the other curves, and the Go, Rust, and assembly outputs
  are not taken.
- The files are not compiled on their own: `xo_p256.c` includes them.
  `fiatcrypto.go` embeds them, and internal/build writes them next to
  the Mbed TLS tree (`fiat-crypto/src/`, an include directory of the
  library build).
- Update: `scripts/vendor-fiat-crypto.sh` (set the commit, run with
  `UPDATE=1` for the new sums, pin them, run again), then
  `go test ./third_party/fiat-crypto ./internal/build` (TestVendored,
  TestTLSAccel) and the TLS tests; record the commit here, in
  `fiatcrypto.go`, and in knowledgebase/infrastructure/toolchain.md.
